pairs.difference: A: the umbrella has red, yellow and orange panels and a pale violet pole against a cyan backdrop. This is the warm-hero-on-cool-backdrop split the real cards use. B: the saucer is near-colorless silver and the only hue on it is a small red dome. In the lens the hull's shadow side turns green-mauve from the green backdrop. The card reads as one green hue family (1.36), below the real range.
pairs.fix: Paint the saucer's hull in a clear local color, such as a warm cream or orange body with darker bands. Keep the red dome and the warm bulbs. Keep the hull's shadow side a darker version of its own color, not green from the background.

pairs.difference: A: a red-and-silver rocket with an orange flame on a blue sky. The warm hero sits against a cool backdrop. B: a white plane with blue stripes and blue engine shadows on a blue sky with white clouds. The hero repeats the background's hue, the card has no warm color (warm share 0.0), and the lens turns the plane's shadows the same blue as the sky.
pairs.fix: Give the plane a warm livery, such as a red or orange tail and a stripe along the body. Paint the engines warm grey, not sky blue, so the plane stands out from the blue sky.

pairs.difference: A: red, orange, teal and violet balloons with orange strings on a blue sky. There are many hues, but each balloon keeps its own local color. B: the saucer is one saturated yellow-orange mass, and its lower half drops into a brown-orange shadow in the lens. Pink-magenta glows under it add a third hue with no role.
pairs.fix: Paint the saucer a softer yellow, with a darker olive-gold shadow underneath instead of orange-brown. Make the glow under the saucer pale yellow-white, not magenta.

pairs.difference: A: the map mixes cream paper, sky-blue water, green islands and a dark grey magnifier on warm wood, with plenty of muted color. B: the star chart is one flat ultramarine slab with white stars and an orange compass. Apart from the wood, the card is two hue masses (2.69 families, below the real range), and the blue reads as pure screen color.
pairs.fix: Paint the star chart a deep navy with soft teal and violet nebula patches. Make the stars warm white and the border aged cream with gold corners, so the chart is not one flat ultramarine block.

pairs.difference: A: a hot-pink tray with pale blue ice on orange wood under a cyan sky. B: pink, yellow and blue pool rings with a yellow duck on yellow-green grass, in front of a brown fence. Both cards stack several pure hues and both reach 5.96 families. Color gives no clear reason to choose.

A: the battery's grey metal caps and its cast shadow turn pink from the backdrop, so the neutral metal loses its own color. Shadow chroma is 0.628, below the real range. The cyan core is the only other hue. B: a blue vending machine on violet, with red, yellow and green cans and bottles that keep their own local colors.
pairs.fix: Paint the battery's caps a neutral steel grey with cool blue-grey shadows, not pink. Put a darker, slightly purple shadow on the floor under the battery.

pairs.difference: A: a sand castle in tan and ochre with a green bucket and blue spade on a blue sea and sky. The shadows stay a rich brown-orange. B: the green bumper car drops into near-black green-grey shadows, and the dark rubber bumper and grey floor are almost colorless. Shadow chroma is 0.343, far below the real range.
pairs.fix: Make the car's shadow side a deep saturated green, not black. Paint the bumper a dark navy or charcoal-blue, and give the floor a light blue-violet tint that picks up some of the orange from the backdrop.

pairs.difference: A: the drone is white and charcoal with almost no color (subject chroma 0.014). Only the blue camera lens adds a hue, and the yellow sunburst fills the rest of the card (warm share 0.998). The lens turns the shadows yellow-brown. B: a dark green lamp with a warm yellow bulb on a turquoise burst. The lamp keeps a dark green local color.
pairs.fix: Give the drone a colored body, such as a red or blue shell with white trim. Make the propellers dark grey-blue and the shadows under the arms cool blue-grey, so the drone stands out against the yellow background.

pairs.difference: A is the real lighthouse from the lessons: a red-and-cream tower against a blue sea and sky. B: a white mast on a grey concrete roof with a tiny red light. In the lens the roof and pole merge into one grey-lilac mass, and the hero has almost no chroma (0.028). The card is pale blue and grey only (warm share 0.005).
pairs.fix: Paint the mast with red-and-white bands and a warm orange beacon. Make the roof warm sandstone or terracotta tiles instead of grey concrete, so the warm hero sits against the blue sky.

pairs.difference: A: the rover, the moon ground and the sky are all lilac-violet. The white rover picks up the same purple in its shadows, so the whole card is one hue family plus a small orange crate (hero chroma 0.04). B: a red bike on a blue car with a warm sunset road. The red, blue and orange are all distinct.
pairs.fix: Paint the rover with a white body plus orange or yellow panels, and keep its shadows neutral warm grey instead of purple. Make the moon ground a cool grey and the sky a deep blue-black, so the purple does not cover everything.

pairs.difference: A: a teal book with red, yellow and blue stickers and pink and blue bookmarks on orange wood. The teal hero sits against a warm backdrop. B: a black tablet with a flat pure-cyan screen on brushed grey metal. The background is almost colorless (chroma 0.023), the shadows go flat grey-black (0.179), and the cyan screen is the only hue on the card.
pairs.fix: Put a colorful app or picture on the tablet screen in place of the flat cyan. Give the tablet a colored case, such as orange or red, and set it on a warm surface like wood or a soft-colored backdrop instead of grey metal.

pairs.difference: A: blue sneakers with green, teal and pink accents on orange and cream. The blue hero sits against a warm backdrop. B: the white helmet takes on the purple of the backdrop in the lens, the gold visor shades to brown-purple, and orange trim is the only accent. That gives 1.79 hue families, and the background chroma of 0.218 is above the real range.
pairs.fix: Keep the helmet shell a clean neutral white with cool grey shadows, not purple. Make the visor deep gold with a dark amber shadow, and tone the violet background down slightly so it is less saturated than the helmet.

pattern: Generated cards most often show one dominant hue spread across both hero and background. Neutral heroes (silver, white, grey) take on the backdrop color in their shadows (purple rover, pink battery caps, purple helmet, green UFO), or the hero repeats the backdrop's hue (blue plane on blue sky). Hue families drop below the real range. Shadows either go colorless grey-black (bumper car, tablet) or become orange-brown versions of the light. Real cards keep the hero's own local color, warm against a cool backdrop, with shadows that are darker but still clearly colored.
